Same-family test is same_family(a, b): name_key(a.head.name) == name_key(b.head.name) and a.head.birth_year == b.head.birth_year. The head is members[0] and birth_year is int(birth_date[:4]).", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "name_key(name) = tuple(soundex(part) for part in name.split()); soundex(word) is American Soundex (first letter + 3 digits, e.g. 'Robert' -> 'R163'), so spelling variants like 'Mohamed'/'Muhammad' map to the same code. This is the matching rule to reuse for finding duplicate families.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "is_valid_household_id(household_id: str) -> bool validates IDs of the form HH-NNNNC via re.fullmatch(r\"HH-(\\d{4})(\\d)\") and household_check_digit(m.group(1)) == int(m.group(2)). household_check_digit(base) computes a mod-11 check digit with CHECK_WEIGHTS = (5, 4, 3, 2) and returns None when the check would be 10 (such bases are never issued). Use this to pick the record with the valid ID.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "registry/register.py set_status(household_id: str, status: str, *, merged_into: str | None = None) -> Household marks a household with status 'active' | 'inactive' | 'merged' (raises ValueError otherwise), sets h.merged_into = merged_into, saves, and returns the Household; raises KeyError if the ID is not found. This is the existing function to mark duplicates as merged without deleting them.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "Registry persistence: load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household] reads all households from data/registry.json (key 'households') via store.read_json(REGISTRY) with REGISTRY = 'registry.json'; save_households(households) writes the whole list back with store.write_json(REGISTRY, {'households': [h.to_dict() for h in households]}). get_household(household_id) raises KeyError if absent.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Household dataclass fields: id, region, site, phone, members (list[Member], members[0] is head), registered (ISO date), status ('active' default), sms_ok, shelter_damaged, income_lost, disability, merged_into (str | None). Household.from_dict(d) / to_dict() convert to/from the JSON dict form; Member has name, birth_date (ISO), pregnant.", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Double rations happen because eligibility checks status: is_eligible returns False only when household.status != 'active'; two active duplicates each qualify. Marking one 'merged' via set_status removes it from rations without deleting it, satisfying 'no record is deleted'.", "file": "eligibility/rules.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "Script conventions: ops scripts live in scripts/ and must add the repo root to sys.path (sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))) so imports like 'from registry.register import ...' work; run from the Lifeline root as 'python scripts/<name>.py'. Scripts that change data/registry.json must say so in their docstring.", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "store.write_json writes atomically: it dumps JSON with indent=2 plus a trailing newline to a .tmp file then os.replace onto the target, so a merge script writing registry.json via save_households is crash-safe. There is deliberately no function to edit or delete lines in append-only files (audit.jsonl, outbox/*).", "file": "core/store.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "next_household_id(households: list[Household] | None = None) -> str exists if a kept record ever needs a new ID: it takes max(int(h.id[3:7])) + 1 (default 999) and skips bases where household_check_digit is None, returning make_household_id(number) = f'HH-{number:04d}{check}'.", "file": "registry/register.py"}]}}
